content:
Republicans are divided after President Donald Trump said Americans who oppose building data centers in their communities would end up “backwards and poor.”

“The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor. If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign,” Trump wrote Monday on Truth Social. “The good news is that there are plenty of other places that want them. If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame.”

The debate over data centers for artificial intelligence has become a key issue in the upcoming midterm elections, with the construction of such facilities garnering vocal bipartisan opposition.

A recent Gallup poll found that seven in 10 Americans oppose constructing data centers in their local area. Those who opposed data centers cited a slew of concerns, including the demand for resources like water and power, impact on property values, increased energy costs and pollution.

Rep. Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.) strongly opposed the president’s statement on Monday, declaring, “I guess I’m backwards and poor.”

Kentucky Republican Rep. Savannah Maddox told followers on X that Trump’s messaging was “concerning.”

“Rural doesn’t mean ‘backwards and poor’ and development doesn’t always equate to being successful and rich,’” the lawmaker wrote. “President Trump wouldn’t be president without the rural voters who inhabit America’s heartland.”

She continued, “It is not wrong of us to question the sudden and wide-scale effort to convert arable land into data centers. We are not stupid for wanting to protect our rural way of life.”

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie (Ky.) and Marjorie Taylor Greene also ripped the president, with the former Georgia congresswoman stating, “Everyone hates data centers.”

Other voices from the right also chimed in.

However, some continued to support Trump’s stance, with a number of MAGA supporters even pushing conspiracy theories that the anti-data center movement is rooted in China’s efforts to win the “AI race.”
